title: 걱정하고 제안하기: 막힐 텐데, 제가 할 테니까
objective: By the end, you can form -(으)ㄹ 텐데 and -(으)ㄹ 테니(까) correctly and choose between them: 텐데 for a guess used as background or contrast, and 테니까 for a reason (a guess or your own intention) before a request or suggestion.
summary: Learn to use -(으)ㄹ 텐데 and -(으)ㄹ 테니(까) to give advice, show concern, and make offers based on a guess or your own plan.

task.title: Choose and complete
task.line: Choose the right form or write it, following the instruction for each question.

forms.when: Verb/adjective stem + ㄹ 텐데 (after a vowel or ㄹ) / 을 텐데 (after a consonant)
forms.means: "It will probably be..., so / but..." Your guess is the background for advice, a question, or a contrast.
forms.example: 퇴근 시간이라 길이 막힐 텐데 지하철을 타는 게 어때요?
forms.exampleMeaning: It's rush hour, so the roads will probably be jammed. How about taking the subway?

forms.when: At the end of a sentence, in conversation
forms.means: "I guess..., (so I'm a bit worried)." A soft guess that shows concern.
forms.example: 지금 가면 식당에 사람이 많을 텐데요.
forms.exampleMeaning: If we go now, the restaurant will probably be crowded.

forms.when: Guessing about something that probably already happened
forms.means: "It probably already..." Often followed by a surprising fact.
forms.example: 버스를 탔으면 벌써 도착했을 텐데 아직 안 왔어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: If he took the bus, he would have arrived already, but he's still not here.

forms.when: After any noun (with or without a final consonant)
forms.example: 지금 점심시간일 텐데 이따가 다시 전화해 보세요.
forms.exampleMeaning: It's probably lunchtime now, so try calling again later.

forms.when: Before a request, suggestion, or advice
forms.means: "Since it will surely..., (do this)." A strong guess is the reason.
forms.example: 점심시간이라 식당이 붐빌 테니까 조금 일찍 나가요.
forms.exampleMeaning: It's lunchtime, so restaurants will be crowded. Let's leave a little early.

forms.means: "I'll do..., so you (do this)." You offer or promise something.
forms.example: 제가 커피를 살 테니까 여기서 기다리세요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I'll buy the coffee, so wait here.

watchOut: 할텐데 (X) → 할 텐데 (O): Always put a space before 텐데 and 테니까. It is spelled 텐데, not 텐대.
더을 텐데 (X) → 더울 텐데 (O): For ㅂ-irregular words, ㅂ changes to 우 first (덥다 → 더울, 춥다 → 추울).
제가 운전할 텐데 쉬세요 (X) → 제가 운전할 테니까 쉬세요 (O): To offer what you will do, use 테니까, not 텐데.
바쁠 테니까 와 줬네요 (X) → 바쁠 텐데 와 줬네요 (O): When what actually happened is different from what you'd expect from your guess, use 텐데. 테니까 only gives a reason.
exercises: Choose the correct form: ① 이 옷은 좀 (작을 텐데 / 작은 텐데) 한번 입어 보세요. ② 그 영화는 재미있을 (텐데 / 테니까) 왜 안 봐요?
Change the word in brackets using -(으)ㄹ 텐데: ① 그 가게는 (비싸다) ____ 다른 데 가 볼까요? ② 역까지 (멀다) ____ 택시를 탈까요? ③ 저분은 (이 동네 사람이다) ____ 길을 물어볼까요?
Fill in the blank with -았/었을 텐데 and 피곤하다: 어제 밤늦게까지 일해서 ____ 오늘 아침 일찍 나왔네요.
Choose the sentence that fits: You want to pay for lunch today and let your friend pay next time. (A) 오늘은 제가 낼 텐데 다음에 사 주세요. (B) 오늘은 제가 낼 테니까 다음에 사 주세요.
Fill in the blank with -(으)ㄹ 테니까 and 춥다: 밤에는 산이 ____ 재킷을 가져가세요.
Put the words in order to make one sentence: 천천히 오세요 / 먼저 / 갈 테니까 / 제가
answers: ① 비쌀 텐데 ② 멀 텐데 ③ 이 동네 사람일 텐데
(B) 오늘은 제가 낼 테니까 다음에 사 주세요.
제가 먼저 갈 테니까 천천히 오세요. (먼저 제가 갈 테니까 천천히 오세요.)
